memo.verdict: Park. Neutral; conviction low, a working hypothesis at the Triaging stage. The park rule applies because trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) is D: the series that would confirm or refute the case are quarterly and semi-annual, the monthly ones are proxies, and the record does not argue otherwise; management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) at C, business quality (E 2, BB 2) at C and transmission (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) at C do not trigger it. The case re-enters on any one of three things: a binding Specialized Services disposal at 8 times EBITA or more with a capital-return plan; two consecutive quarters of Core organic growth of +2 percent or more excluding Trust & Safety with FY2027 restructuring guided below EUR 50 million; or a price below about EUR 64, where the modal path alone clears the eighteen-month bar. It is invalidated by FY2027 restructuring guidance above EUR 140 million, a quarter of Core organic growth below -2 percent, or a statement that LanguageLine is not for sale. The one-line bet: a new, aligned management sells part of a 33-percent-margin franchise at a multiple the market will not give the whole, while the core stops shrinking; if neither happens we are paid 6.3 percent to wait on a 4 percent grower at five times earnings. The record's own summary of the situation: the right people have arrived at the right price in the wrong value chain, and the return above the bar is in a sale they have not yet made.
case: - Teleperformance is a self-help and sum-of-the-parts case in a business the market prices as terminal, not a growth case. At EUR 71.80 the shares pay a covered 6.3 percent dividend yield to wait for a disposal that has not been made; on the modal path the return is 11.5 percent a year over eighteen months, a D against the 20 percent bar, and the case clears the bar only on the one-in-three branch where a sale of Specialized Services assets re-rates the whole.

- The change is internal, broad and seven months old. The founder who ran the company for 48 years left in March 2026. Jorge Amar, an AI-native consultant, became chief executive on 2026-03-16 and acted within 100 days: a review of every segment, the restructuring programme expanded to EUR 150 to 170 million of run-rate savings, 70 days of client visits. Moulay Hafid Elalamy became Chairman, separating the roles, and put up to EUR 355 million of his own capital behind the stock through a swap on 2026-03-02 at the point of maximum pessimism (the shares down 60 percent from peak, 55 percent below the five-year average multiple), against a peer insider median of 0.9 percent at Concentrix. A permanent finance director, a chief AI officer, a new Specialized Services chief executive, a new head of investor relations and four new directors followed. The screen's red flags do not fit: EUR 109 million of restructuring cash was booked in H1 2026, acquisitions have stopped, the appointment is permanent. Weaknesses: zero BPO profit-and-loss tenure against a peer operator median of 11 years; the founder stays 18 months as adviser; the former deputy chief executive sits on the board; chronic deputy-chief-executive churn (Mackenbrock resigned 2026-03-15 after seventeen months; Bhupender Singh left abruptly in August 2024); clustered executive selling in August and September 2026.

- The plan is what every sell-side house asked for: EUR 150 to 170 million of cost out, outcome-based pricing (over 15 percent of group revenue, growing mid-single-digit), exit of low-margin countries and contracts, deleveraging to 1.2x by FY2028, and a portfolio review naming LanguageLine, TLScontact and Health Advocate as under review for sale; AllianceOne and TP Infinity USA moved from Specialized to Core from 2026-01-01, the tidy-up a seller does; the Russian subsidiary was sold in December 2025. Internal forces rate B: chief executive B, other leaders B, strategy change B, the reference shareholder's commitment B (the catch-all), standards improvement C, perimeter reduction C (announced and begun at the edges; nothing material sold in seven months), shareholder returns C (dividend held at EUR 4.50; the EUR 150 million 2025 buyback stopped), new products C (TP.ai over 1,100 projects; Data Services for AI growing double-digit; monetisation contested), guidance raised D (rebased down: free cash flow from EUR 1.1 billion in FY2024 to about EUR 800 to 850 million), balance sheet D (utilisation reduced), acquisitions D (stepped down to bolt-ons and minority stakes), new geographies D (delivery-side only), price rises F (falling in nominal and real terms: automation discounts 5 to 10 percent, renewal discounts 15 to 25 percent, offshoring lowering billing rates 20 to 30 percent; management concedes the pressure).
counter_case: - The hypothesis at its strongest, the risk research's winning profile of a false friend: the quarterly stability we would use to confirm the case (a sequential improvement, a held margin, strong normalised cash) is produced by offshoring gains and consolidation accounting that mask a core whose contract values are deflating permanently. Clients move from seat-based to outcome-based pricing and keep the automation savings; a former Concentrix director's example is a USD 5 million human contract falling to USD 400,000 or less. The EUR 120 to 140 million of annual restructuring is the operating cost of that deflation, so the adjusted earnings on which the 4.9 times multiple is struck overstate true earnings by about a third: EUR 284 million of adjustments in 2025, 25 percent of reported profit against a 15 to 18 percent industry median. Specialized Services, the asset the bull wants sold, has itself just lost a visa contract and shrank 3.9 percent like-for-like in H1 2026, and its 330-basis-point margin jump to 33.0 percent was temporary price negotiation on an expert's reading. The consultant chief executive has no record in low-margin human operations. The disposal, if it comes, sells the one franchise automation does not reach and leaves shareholders holding the deflating core: a one-time event that removes the reason to own the rest. Deutsche Bank's 12.7 percent FY2028 margin and Morgan Stanley's EUR 10 bear case are this hypothesis in numbers.

- What the record concedes: the adjusted basis is flattered, and treating restructuring as recurring takes the modal return to an F (4.3 percent a year over eighteen months); the Specialized margin jump may be partly temporary; the leading indicators are quarterly and the hypothesis is designed to pass them; the price has already moved 68 percent from the low on inputs alone; no disposal has been signed in seven months.
triggers: - Re-entry on any one of: a binding Specialized Services disposal at 8 times EBITA or more with a capital-return plan; two consecutive quarters of Core organic growth of +2 percent or more excluding Trust & Safety with FY2027 restructuring guided below EUR 50 million; a price below about EUR 64 (EUR 64.3 on the eighteen-month arithmetic; EUR 55.8 for the three-year bar).
- Invalidation on any one of: FY2027 restructuring guidance above EUR 140 million; a quarter of Core organic growth below -2 percent; a statement that LanguageLine is not for sale.

- The disposal branch's odds move to probable on a binding agreement and to unlikely on a statement that LanguageLine is core; the savings-retention view moves to probable on an H1 2027 recurring EBITA margin of 15 percent or more and to unlikely on FY2027 restructuring guidance above EUR 140 million; the adjusted-basis view moves on FY2027 restructuring guidance of EUR 100 million or more (a third year above that level) or below EUR 50 million.

- Alarm levels: the portfolio review passing the FY2026 results (2027-02-18) with no conclusion; a quarter of Core organic growth below zero after H2 2026; the FY2026 recurring EBITA margin below 14.6 percent; a top-ten client insourcing or automating in one move; a nationwide Philippine wage rise enacted or a further Colombian labour law; FY2027 restructuring guidance of EUR 100 million or more; average contract duration falling below three years toward two; the Specialized margin below 30 percent; the outcome-based share below 20 percent at end-2027; a further deputy or divisional departure.

- Dated steps: the Q3 2026 revenue release (date not in the research); the FY2026 results and FY2027 guide on 2027-02-18; regional employee boards by end-2026; the former finance director's term ending 2026-12-31; the founder's advisory term ending September 2027; H1 2027 results showing whether the EUR 150 to 170 million of savings are in the margin; the outcome-based mix test of 25 to 30 percent of sales by Q4 2027; the FY2028 targets (4 to 6 percent organic growth, about 15.5 percent margin, 1.2x leverage, EUR 3 billion cumulative free cash flow) falling due; the first LTIP vesting at free cash flow over EUR 2.3 billion.

- Open questions the record could not close: whether the Specialized margin jump to 33.0 percent is a run rate or temporary price negotiation; whether lower capex (1.9 percent of revenue) is efficiency or under-investment; whether the doubling of ethics-hotline reports to 3,340 in 2025 is better reporting or worse conduct; whether the most advantaged next-cycle competitor is technology-first rather than the largest; the size of the data-labelling line, which no figure in the research gives; the own-errors overlap (KQ 1, RA 7, E 1, BB 4), unanswerable because the framework's track-record and lessons files were not supplied; contract durations, undisclosed and known only from expert calls.
